title: A storm leaves Chennai fighting for capacity
story: Heavy northeast monsoon rains cause severe rain fade on emulated satellite links while multiple essential services compete for degraded backhaul bandwidth.
human_decisions: Commander establishes temporary capacity priority order: 112 calls first, hospitals second, power grid third, general commercial shed.
Commander clarifies that priority allocation is an operational decision rather than statutory command.
Commander approves PB-10 downstream warning drafted by Gap Analyst.

objective.what: Priority queuing and domestic gateway failover restore critical traffic during monsoon rain fade.

schedule.what: M1 detects rising traffic and packet loss during heavy monsoon rain.
M2 forecasts severe rain fade and reduced link margin.
M3 evaluates degradation pattern as weather-induced fade.
M2 predicts battery exhaustion at coastal tower CHN-05 following mains interruption.
Gap Analyst audits statutory minimum battery backup runtime requirements.
M4 requests legally binding capacity allocation and priority rules.
Commander establishes a temporary operational priority order: 112 calls first, hospitals second, grid third.
Power utility restores mains at coastal tower CHN-05 before its battery reaches the cut-off.
Mobile operator fails over coastal site CHN-05 to domestic backup gateway.
Mobile operator executes PB-10 to alert downstream emergency services after commander approval.
M1 sees the rain band move inland; rain stops at the monitored sites.
M1 confirms critical traffic delivery restored on prioritized queues.
